Dataset: magicsword001/robust-edit · Notebook (31B A/B): robust-edit: reliable edits for Gemma 4 agents · Apache 2.0

While reading 31B traces we kept seeing the agent lose tool calls to editing rather than to reasoning. A lot of that comes from the harness, not the model, and a submission can route around it. robust-edit is the result: a skill you copy into your submission, plus a one-call setup step.

What goes wrong today (swegemma 0.2.7, wheelhouse 2026-09-30)

  1. edit_file loses arguments on 31B. The model sometimes closes a string argument with a backtick ("filepath": "src/x.py\,old_string:"), andold_string/new_stringdisappear. Across three runs of 16 tasks, 107 of 246edit_filecalls (43%) failed, most of them this way, often in streaks of the same broken call. Tools with a single string argument (run_command`) did not lose arguments in our runs.
  2. Copied escapes. Tool results reach the model as one level of JSON, so code appears with \n and \". Models copy them into old_string, often as a backslash followed by a real line break, which the unescaped fallback in adk_eval_core does not undo (very common on our 12B proxy, rare on 31B).
  3. Repeated identical calls after a failed edit (up to 24 in a row in our traces).
  4. Edited test files sink correct fixes. The reset of agent-edited test files before the hidden test patch is a no-op (744825), so one edited test file makes the test patch fail to apply. We saw this on 31B too.

What robust-edit does

A setup step (one run_skill_script call) installs a small editor at .git/agent/edit.py (invisible to the patch) and marks test/config files skip-worktree. The agent edits with one run_command:

python3 .git/agent/edit.py path/to/file.py <<'EOF'
<<<<<<< SEARCH
lines currently in the file
=======
new lines
>>>>>>> REPLACE
EOF
  • matches exact text first, then ignoring whitespace/indentation, then with copied escapes undone (and applies the same repair to the replacement);
  • refuses an edit that would leave a Python file that does not compile, and shows the error in context;
  • on a miss, returns the closest lines with line numbers (and --lines A-B to replace by line numbers); says so when nothing would change or the same edit already failed;
  • standard library only; works in the Docker and the subprocess sandbox.

Results (31B, 4×L4, 16 training tasks, 40 calls / 20 min, three runs)

Each run compares two agents that differ only in robust-edit, alternately on the same tasks. The public notebook reruns the comparison with the generic agent shipped in the dataset.

without robust-edit with robust-edit
edit_file failures 107 of 246 (43%) 19 of 66 (29%)
editor failures – 8 of 75 (11%)
setup step ran – 47 of 48
tasks lost to an edited test file 3 0
resolved 6/16 in every run 6/16 in every run

The editor never lost arguments or failed on copied escapes; its non-applied edits are mostly correct refusals (a syntax-breaking edit, SEARCH text that really is not in the file, a budget stop). The agent still chooses edit_file for part of its edits (from 16% to 70% depending on the prompt), and those fail as usual. It did not change the number of resolved tasks in these samples; it removes wasted calls and turns and a class of silent losses (broken files, edited tests — one of the three tasks lost that way was resolved with robust-edit).

Two things we learned on the way that may save you time:

  • Skill scripts must not hard-code /workspace. In the subprocess sandbox the repository is a temporary directory, and ADK runs skill scripts after chdir into a temporary copy of the skill. Our first version silently did nothing on Kaggle. setup.py shows how to find the repository.
  • "First, call X" in the prompt is not reliable. 31B skipped such a setup instruction in 11 of 16 tasks. A SequentialAgent with a one-call setup step in front of the solver ran it in 47 of 48 tasks. Give that step the same tool list as the solver (an unknown tool call is fatal in ADK, and the harness's task prompt mentions all tools) and keep thinking on with a small budget.

Using it

Copy skills/robust-edit/ into your submission, put the setup step in front of your agent (example/ is a complete submission), put the editor into the fix step of your prompt as in example/prompts/solver.md (where it is mentioned changes how often the agent uses it), and keep edit_file in the tool list. Details and limitations are in the README.

Feedback and failure cases are welcome — if the editor refuses or mangles something it should not, a trace excerpt will help us fix it.
